statement: Similar pyramids which have triangular bases are in the triplicate ratio of their corresponding sides.
heath_proof: Let there be similar and similarly situated pyramids of which the triangles ABC, DEF, are the bases and the points G, H the vertices; I say that the pyramid ABCG has to the pyramid DEFH the ratio triplicate of that which BC has to EF. For let the parallelepipedal solids BGML, EHQP be completed. Now, since the pyramid ABCG is similar to the pyramid DEFH, therefore the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF, the angle GBC to the angle HEF, and the angle ABG to the angle DEH; and, as AB is to DE, so is BC to EF, and BG to EH. And since, as AB is to DE, so is BC to EF, and the sides are proportional about equal angles, therefore the parallelogram BM is similar to the parallelogram EQ. For the same reason BN is also similar to ER, and BK to EO; therefore the three parallelograms MB, BK, BN are similar to the three EQ, EO, ER. But the three parallelograms MB, BK, BN are equal and similar to their three opposites, and the three EQ, EO, ER are equal and similar to their three opposites. [XI. 24] Therefore the solids BGML, EHQP are contained by similar planes equal in multitude. Therefore the solid BGML is similar to the solid EHQP. But similar parallelepipedal solids are in the triplicate ratio of their corresponding sides. [XI. 33] Therefore the solid BGML has to the solid EHQP the ratio triplicate of that which the corresponding side BC has to the corresponding side EF. But, as the solid BGML is to the solid EHQP, so is the pyramid ABCG to the pyramid DEFH, inasmuch as the pyramid is a sixth part of the solid, because the prism which is half of the parallelepipedal solid [XI. 28] is also triple of the pyramid. [XII. 7] Therefore the pyramid ABCG also has to the pyramid DEFH the ratio triplicate of that which BC has to EF.
ai_proof_text:
12.8
**Statement:** Similar pyramids which have triangular bases are in the triplicate ratio of their corresponding sides.

**Step 1.** Let ABCG and DEFH be similar pyramids with triangular bases ABC, DEF and vertices G, H, the vertices A, B, C, G corresponding to D, E, F, H respectively, so that BC and EF are corresponding sides. I say that the pyramid ABCG has to the pyramid DEFH the ratio triplicate of that which BC has to EF.

**Step 2.** Since the pyramids are similar, they are contained by similar planes equal in multitude (D11.9); thus the triangle ABC is similar to the triangle DEF, the triangle GBC to the triangle HEF, and the triangle ABG to the triangle DEH. Therefore, by the definition of similar rectilineal figures (D6.1), the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF, the angle CBG to the angle FEH, and the angle ABG to the angle DEH; and the sides about these equal angles are proportional: as AB is to BC, so is DE to EF; as BC is to BG, so is EF to EH; and as AB is to BG, so is DE to EH.

**Step 3.** Through A draw AK parallel to BC and through C draw CK parallel to BA (1.31), so that BAKC is a parallelogram on the sides BA, BC; in the same manner complete the parallelogram BCMG on BC, BG and the parallelogram BGNA on BG, BA; and let the parallelepipedal solid BL be completed, having these three parallelograms about the solid angle at B and L as the vertex opposite B, so that its remaining faces are the parallelograms GNLM, AKLN, CMLK, opposite to BAKC, BCMG, BGNA respectively. Likewise complete the parallelograms EDPF on ED, EF; EFQH on EF, EH; EHRD on EH, ED; and the parallelepipedal solid EO with O the vertex opposite E, whose remaining faces are HROQ, DPOR, FQOP, opposite to EDPF, EFQH, EHRD respectively.

**Step 4.** The parallelogram BAKC is similar to the parallelogram EDPF. For the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF (Step 2). The opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal (1.34), so the angle AKC is equal to the angle ABC and the angle DPF to the angle DEF; hence the angle AKC is equal to the angle DPF (CN1). Again, since AK is parallel to BC and BA falls upon them, the interior angles BAK, ABC are together equal to two right angles (1.29); likewise the angles EDP, DEF are together equal to two right angles; and the angles ABC, DEF being equal, the angle BAK is equal to the angle EDP (CN3). In the same way the angle BCK is equal to the angle EFP. Thus the two parallelograms have their angles severally equal. Moreover, as AB is to BC, so is DE to EF (Step 2), and the opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal (1.34), AK being equal to BC, KC to BA, DP to EF and PF to ED; hence the sides about all the equal angles are proportional. Therefore the parallelogram BAKC is similar to the parallelogram EDPF (D6.1).

**Step 5.** For the same reason, since the angle CBG is equal to the angle FEH and as BC is to BG so is EF to EH, the parallelogram BCMG is similar to the parallelogram EFQH; and since the angle ABG is equal to the angle DEH and as AB is to BG so is DE to EH, the parallelogram BGNA is similar to the parallelogram EHRD.

**Step 6.** Now the opposite planes of a parallelepipedal solid are equal and similar parallelograms (11.24). Therefore GNLM is equal and similar to BAKC, AKLN to BCMG, and CMLK to BGNA; and HROQ is equal and similar to EDPF, DPOR to EFQH, and FQOP to EHRD. Since figures which are similar to the same rectilineal figure are also similar to one another (6.21), GNLM is similar to EDPF, and hence to HROQ; and likewise AKLN is similar to DPOR, and CMLK to FQOP.

**Step 7.** Therefore the six faces of the solid BL are severally similar to the six faces of the solid EO; that is, the solids BL, EO are contained by similar planes equal in multitude, so that the solid BL is similar to the solid EO (D11.9); and BC, EF are corresponding sides of them, being the sides about the equal angles ABC, DEF in the similar faces BAKC, EDPF.

**Step 8.** But similar parallelepipedal solids are to one another in the triplicate ratio of their corresponding sides (11.33). Therefore the solid BL has to the solid EO the ratio triplicate of that which BC has to EF.

**Step 9.** Next, the solid BL is cut by the plane through AC and NM, the diagonals of the opposite faces BAKC, GNLM; and a parallelepipedal solid cut by a plane through the diagonals of opposite planes is bisected by that plane (11.28), the two halves being prisms with triangular bases. One of these halves is the prism having the triangle ABC as base and the triangle NGM as the opposite face, with AN, BG, CM as its parallel edges. Therefore the solid BL is double of this prism.

**Step 10.** Again, any prism with a triangular base is divided into three pyramids equal to one another with triangular bases, so that a pyramid is a third part of the prism which has the same base and equal height with it (12.7). The pyramid ABCG has the same base ABC as this prism, and its vertex G lies in the face NGM opposite the base, so that it has the same height as the prism; hence the prism is triple of the pyramid ABCG. Consequently the solid BL is six times the pyramid ABCG.

**Step 11.** In the same way the solid EO is bisected by the plane through DF and RQ, the diagonals of the opposite faces EDPF, HROQ, into two equal prisms (11.28), one of which has the triangle DEF as base and the triangle RHQ as the opposite face; and the pyramid DEFH, having the same base DEF and the same height as this prism, is a third part of it (12.7). Therefore the solid EO is six times the pyramid DEFH.

**Step 12.** Thus the solids BL, EO are the same multiples, namely sextuples, of the pyramids ABCG, DEFH respectively; and parts have the same ratio as the same multiples of them taken in corresponding order (5.15). Therefore, as the pyramid ABCG is to the pyramid DEFH, so is the solid BL to the solid EO.

**Step 13.** But the solid BL has to the solid EO the ratio triplicate of that which BC has to EF (Step 8); and ratios which are the same with the same ratio are also the same with one another (5.11). Therefore the pyramid ABCG also has to the pyramid DEFH the ratio triplicate of that which the corresponding side BC has to the corresponding side EF. Hence similar pyramids which have triangular bases are in the triplicate ratio of their corresponding sides. Q.E.D.
